heading: Graphs Have Cycles, Trees Don't
body:
**Key difference:** Graphs can contain cycles (paths that loop back).

**Critical rule:** Always use a `visited` set when doing DFS on graphs.

Without it? Infinite loops. With it? Each node processed exactly once.

Trees never need this because they're acyclic by definition.

heading: Neighbors = Adjacency List
body:
Graph representation:
- **Adjacency list:** `{node: [neighbors]}`
- Most common in interviews

Quickly finding neighbors is the whole game.

`graph[node]` gives you all neighbors in O(1).

label: DFS with Visited · Python

q: Why is a visited set necessary when performing DFS on a graph but not on a tree?
options: Graphs can contain cycles, which could cause infinite loops without tracking visited nodes
Trees are always smaller than graphs, so they don't need optimization
Graphs always have more edges than trees
Trees use recursion but graphs use iteration
explain: Graphs can have cycles that loop infinitely. Trees are acyclic by definition, so no visited set needed.
